entries.05446f20600a7332: This is a reportable segment that provides solutions optimizing the entire global supply chain of corporate customers by combining international forwarding, international express, contract logistics overseas and other services. Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., Kobe Yamato Co., Ltd., Konan Kogyo Co., Ltd., YAMATO TRANSPORT U.S.A., INC., YAMATO TRANSPORT EUROPE B.V., YAMATO TRANSPORT (S) PTE. LTD., YAMATO TRANSPORT (M) SDN. BHD., Yamato Logistics Management (China) Co., Ltd., Yamato International Logistics Co., Ltd., Yamato Transport (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd., TAIWAN YAMATO INTERNATIONAL LOGISTICS INC. and others are responsible for the segment. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥97,552 million (up 13.5% year on year). The breakdown is logistics support revenue of ¥134,774 million, transportation revenue of ¥6,243 million, other revenue of ¥4,560 million, and intersegment eliminations of −¥48,025 million. The company explains that the increase in revenue was due to progress in expanding international forwarding sales. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥8,150 million, the largest among the reportable segments, a decrease of ¥877 million year on year. Segment assets were ¥62,100 million, and the number of employees was 2,770. The company states that, while leveraging the vast domestic customer base built through Takkyubin, it is working to further expand in areas where it has strengths, such as automotive, high-tech and food industries, and is strengthening its sales capabilities mainly in Japan, North America, China and Southeast Asia. In January 2026, to support the construction of global supply chains for manufacturers aiming to expand production in India, the Yamato Group opened its largest overseas logistics center. Because revenue from external customers in Japan exceeds 90% of consolidated operating revenue, information by region is omitted.
entries.0a6360f70f9760b1: The company positions its Takkyubin delivery network as social infrastructure. In January 1976, it launched the Takkyubin service, a home-delivery system for small parcels; in November 1997, service began in the Ogasawara Islands, completing the nationwide Takkyubin network; and in December 1996, it began Takkyubin operations during the year-end and New Year holidays, making its operations 365 days a year. In September 2013, it completed "Haneda Chronogate," an integrated logistics terminal. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, the company made capital expenditures of ¥69,446 million (including security deposits), centered on growth investments aimed at improving transport efficiency to strengthen the Takkyubin network and expanding the value it provides across the entire supply chain. In the Express Business, it spent ¥48,794 million on items including renovation work for tenant occupancy at DPL Tokyo Shinonome, the acquisition of the Shiomibashi Building and vehicle purchases; in the Contract Logistics Business, it spent ¥15,745 million on items including construction of logistics facilities and renovation work at various sites. On the safety front, Yamato Transport Co., Ltd. has been progressively renewing drive recorders on approximately 46,000 collection and delivery vehicles since October 2025, aiming to improve safety awareness and driving skills through visualization of driving conditions. As bases combining warehousing and transport, in October 2025 it opened an integrated business solutions base in Koriyama City, Fukushima Prefecture, and in January 2026 it opened, in India, the Yamato Group's largest overseas logistics center.

entries.3299f89da0ecb670: The head office is located at Ginza Nichome 16-10, Chuo-ku, Tokyo. Its predecessor, Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., was founded on November 29, 1919 in Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo City, with capital of ¥100,000 and 4 vehicles. In October 1982 the company name was changed from Yamato Transport Co., Ltd. to Yamato Transport Co., Ltd. (new), and in November 2005, with the move to a pure holding company, the name was changed from Yamato Transport Co., Ltd. to YAMATO HOLDINGS CO., LTD., and the delivery business and others were succeeded to Yamato Transport Split Preparation Co., Ltd. (now Yamato Transport Co., Ltd.). The corporate group consists of 45 subsidiaries and 12 affiliates. As of March 31, 2026, the number of consolidated employees is 174,696, with full-time employees at 87,347 and part-time employees at 87,349, almost the same number. By segment, there are 157,902 in the Express Business, 7,603 in the Contract Logistics Business, 4,407 in Other, 2,770 in the Global Business, 1,996 in the Mobility Business and 18 in corporate. The filing company alone has 18 employees (average age 36.4 years, average length of service 10.3 years), and the company explains that, because it is a pure holding company, the employees belonging to it are mainly personnel who perform management functions. The company with the most employees is Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., with 76,882 full-time employees (average age 45.9 years, average length of service 17.3 years) and 83,491 part-time employees. Labor unions such as the Yamato Transport Labor Union are organized in the Yamato Group. The company falls under a specified listed company, etc. as provided in Article 49, Paragraph 2 of the Cabinet Office Order on Regulation of Securities Transactions.

entries.37c30a7082d7c91f: Consolidated operating revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,865,675 million, an increase of ¥102,979 million (5.8%) from the prior year. entries.94b1f74a1409c735: This is a reportable segment that provides solutions to help corporate customers solve problems and grow their businesses, by combining transportation and delivery networks with added-value functions such as warehouse operations. Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., Nakano Shokai Co., Ltd., IS Tosu Development No. 2 Special Purpose Company and others are responsible for the segment. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥164,602 million (up 69.6% year on year). The breakdown is transportation revenue of ¥54,612 million (up 190.1%), logistics support revenue of ¥117,231 million (up 43.1%), other revenue of ¥16,822 million, and intersegment eliminations of −¥24,063 million. The company explains that this increase in revenue was due to progress in winning new projects and to the conversion of Nakano Shokai Co., Ltd. into a consolidated subsidiary, among other factors. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥6,217 million (up ¥634 million year on year). However, in the current fiscal year, the segment recorded goodwill amortization of ¥14,906 million (of which ¥13,434 million was recorded as "goodwill amortization" in extraordinary losses) in connection with the evaluation of goodwill, and the year-end balance of goodwill fell from ¥15,827 million at the end of the prior year to ¥920 million. The segment also recorded an impairment loss on fixed assets of ¥1,030 million. Segment assets were ¥99,913 million, the number of employees was 7,603, and capital expenditure was ¥15,745 million, including construction of logistics facilities and renovation work at various bases. In October 2025, the company opened an integrated business solutions base in Koriyama City, Fukushima Prefecture, which combines a transport terminal of the Yamato Group with a logistics center that has high added-value functions.
entries.95dabc7163868e2c: The Yamato Group's corporate philosophy is to contribute to the realization of an affluent society through advancing the Takkyubin network as social infrastructure, creating more convenient and comfortable living-related services, and developing innovative logistics systems. YAMATO HOLDINGS CO., LTD. is a pure holding company, and its corporate group consists of 45 subsidiaries and 12 affiliates. There are four reportable segments (the Express Business, Contract Logistics Business, Global Business and Mobility Business), and in addition, 'Other', which is not included in the reportable segments. Revenue is heavily concentrated in domestic parcel delivery: operating revenue from external customers in the Express Business for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,557,978 million, accounting for 83.5% of consolidated operating revenue of ¥1,865,675 million, and the related information breaks this down into ¥1,408,896 million for parcel delivery (Takkyubin) and ¥456,778 million for other. Because operating revenue from external customers in Japan exceeds 90% of consolidated operating revenue, information by region is not disclosed, and there is also no specific customer accounting for 10% or more of consolidated operating revenue. The company positions its medium-term management plan 'Sustainability Transformation 2030 ～1st Stage～', with the fiscal year ending March 2027 as its final year, as 'a 3-year period to strengthen the Takkyubin network and transform the business portfolio.' In the core domain, while the parcel delivery market is trending upward along with the growth of ＥＣ, the market for individuals and small corporate customers is affected by population decline and sluggish personal consumption; with the progress of ＥＣ and changes in demographics, the volume of collection and delivery work in the last-mile domain and the flow of parcels between urban and rural areas are changing, and the company says the profitability of the Takkyubin network is trending downward. Accordingly, it is advancing appropriate pass-through of cost increases through appropriate pricing for large corporate customers and the revision of Takkyubin notified rates in October 2025; in the transportation domain, it is working on reviewing delivery methods in line with changes in parcel flows and on the appropriate allocation of workers responsible for sorting. The growth domain is business for corporations: the Contract Logistics Business recorded a 69.6% increase in revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026, also drawing on the know-how of Nakano Shokai Co., Ltd., which became a consolidated subsidiary in December 2024, and the Global Business recorded a 13.5% increase in revenue, driven by expanded sales of international forwarding. For these two businesses, the company says it will utilize M&A and strategic business alliances in addition to autonomous growth measures. The new domain provides to outside parties, as a 'Green Mobility' business model, know-how accumulated through environmental investment and demonstration tests within the group; the listed initiatives are expanded sales of 'ＥＶ Life Cycle Service', supply of renewable energy centered on Yamato Energy Management Co., Ltd., deployment of an open platform for joint transport and delivery, and health management support services for motor carriers. Payment is collected generally within 30 to 70 days from the point of revenue recognition for contractual consideration for services provided, and for transport services to individual customers and others in the Express Business, payment is collected at the time the cargo is accepted. On the financial side, the company says it is strengthening balance sheet management and will consider monetization of fixed assets as appropriate; in the fiscal year ended March 2026, Yamato Transport Co., Ltd. sold the Konan Biru in Minato-ku, Tokyo, and 19 other properties, partly using sale-and-leaseback transactions, and also partly switched vehicle procurement to leasing.

entries.b4ffec0e6c754935: This reportable segment provides vehicle maintenance services that support safe operation by transport operators and expand vehicle operating hours without stopping vehicles, and supplies renewable electricity and other power used for EVs. It is run by Yamato Auto Works Co., Ltd., its regional companies (Iwate, Hokushinetsu, Shikoku and Okinawa), and Yamato Energy Management Co., Ltd. Operating revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥22,033 million (up 7.5% year on year), which the company attributes to an increase in the number of contracted vehicles as well as the collection of appropriate fees. Intersegment internal operating revenue or transfers amounted to ¥44,401 million, and operating revenue including these was ¥66,435 million, a structure in which vehicle maintenance within the group accounts for a large share. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥5,221 million (up ¥1,440 million year on year), which the company attributes to, among other things, its focus on optimizing costs. Segment assets were ¥53,959 million, and the number of employees was 1,996. The company says it is promoting sales of the “EV Life Cycle Service,” which packages, in addition to vehicle maintenance services, know-how on EV procurement and efficient use, the supply of renewable energy-derived electricity, and the energy management system developed within the Yamato Group, drawing on know-how in EVs, solar power generation equipment and energy management that it has accumulated through environmental investment and demonstration projects within the Yamato Group.

In the related information "Information by product and service," operating revenues from external customers are divided into ¥1,408,896 million for home delivery and ¥456,778 million for others. The company focuses on creating an environment in which sales drivers can devote themselves to facing customers and providing better service, and is advancing the relocation of collection and delivery bases based on regional market potential and the rollout of community-based service bases that offer services beyond sending and receiving Takkyubin. Expanding the provision of the "leave-at-door" service in cooperation with EC operators is also cited as an initiative that contributes to reducing redelivery, making logistics more efficient and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The company states that although the home delivery market is on an expanding trend along with the growth of EC, the market for individuals and small-lot corporate customers, its base area, is affected by population decline and weak personal consumption, and the profitability of the Takkyubin network is on a declining trend.

entries.ffc93c6e50170d63: This is a reportable segment that provides domestic transport and delivery services centered on TA-Q-BIN to individual and corporate customers. It is carried out mainly by Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., together with Okinawa Yamato Transport Co., Ltd., Yamato Box Charter Co., Ltd., Yamato Multi Charter Co., Ltd., Box Charter Co., Ltd., Sustainable Shared Transport Inc., RH Co., Ltd., Redhorse Corporation, Packcity Japan K.K. and others. Segment assets were ¥970,538 million (including ¥370,128 million for the head office divisions of Yamato Transport Co., Ltd.), and the number of employees was 157,902 (76,551 full-timers and 81,351 part-timers), accounting for 9-tenths of the consolidated number of employees, with capital investment of ¥48,794 million.
